Name: Solar_PV_Location
Title: Where are the PV's located
Description: For France, you can see all the rooftop PV installations (Overlay->France ARTD Polygons) created by G. Kasmi (U de Mines de Paris) along with the building footprints which are best adjusted to 50% opacity so you can see the underlying building roofs in the ESRI world image. For England and Wales, rooftop slopes suitable for PV placement (some of which have already been placed) have been calculated from 1m lidar data. All large rural farms with areas in excess of 200 sq.m. are displayed as red polygons in context (ESRI® sub-metre background image, OSM Power Infrastructure, OSM Buildings). Overlay layers will switch on the Open Infrastructure Map, building footprints and LWM. 3. Plan your solar farm with agrivoltaics This indicator allows you to define a rectangular area (using the usual shift-click and expand right down or up) for planning the location of a new solar farm. By default, the Overlay layers will switch on the Open Infrastructure Map, and the Environmentally Sensitive Regions (Natural Landscapes, National Parks and Sites of Special Scientific Interest) as well as the LWM (Land Water mask). In the data layers switch on the BFG (Bi-Facial Gain) and only for England switch on the VOM canopy height. For other areas, switch on the Meta-CHM although you should be aware that the heights here are biase high compared with the VOM. This will allow you to ensure that your solar farm will not intersect any tree shadow. You can also switch on the Total productivity if you preferentially want to look at regions with low productivity.
